category: Scope and strategic industrial objectives
summary: Defines the framework's objectives and coverage: industrial capacity, competitiveness, resilience and decarbonisation. Amendments address the activities, sectors and policy objectives brought within the Regulation.

category: Manufacturing share of EU GDP
summary: Sets the objective for manufacturing to account for at least 20% of EU GDP by 2035. Amendments concern the target, its framing and the industrial, social or environmental conditions accompanying it.

category: Definitions and eligibility boundaries
summary: Defines the projects, products, technologies, economic operators and investment concepts used throughout the Regulation. Changes to these definitions affect which activities and actors qualify for permitting, demand measures and investment obligations.

category: Administrative coordination and digital permitting
summary: Establishes national single access points for industrial manufacturing applications. Covers their coordinating role, digital interfaces, information exchange and interaction with existing national, regional and local authorities.

category: Streamlined industrial permitting
summary: Establishes a single application and permit-granting procedure for industrial manufacturing projects. Covers procedural coordination, application handling, deadlines and administrative arrangements for granting the required permits.

category: Accelerated permitting for industrial decarbonisation
summary: Extends selected Net-Zero Industry Act permitting provisions to energy-intensive industry decarbonisation projects. Covers eligibility, strategic-project treatment and the conditions under which those projects benefit from accelerated procedures.

category: EU origin and domestic value creation
summary: Defines Union-origin content and the rules used to determine origin. Covers the treatment of production and transformation in the EU, domestic value creation and safeguards against qualifying content through insufficient processing.

section: Article 8 — Content equivalent to Union origin in public procurement
category: Third-country equivalence in procurement
summary: Determines when content from third countries can count as Union-origin content for procurement requirements. Covers international procurement commitments, conditions for equivalence and grounds for excluding particular countries or products.

section: Article 9 — Content equivalent to Union origin in other forms of public intervention
category: Third-country equivalence in public support
summary: Determines when third-country content qualifies as equivalent to Union origin under public support measures. Covers trade-agreement coverage, market access conditions, strategic dependencies and exceptions to equivalence.

category: Low-carbon criteria and emissions verification
summary: Establishes how products qualify as low-carbon, including links to product legislation and emissions methodologies. Covers thresholds, verification, treatment of production inputs and the recognition of recycled or secondary materials.

category: Procurement requirements and derogations
summary: Sets procurement access and product requirements for the covered strategic sectors. Covers application of EU-origin and low-carbon conditions, exemptions for unavailable or unsuitable products, disproportionate costs and additional safeguards attached to procurement.

section: Article 12 — Other forms of public intervention
category: Conditionality of public support schemes
summary: Requires public support schemes to apply the relevant product and origin conditions. Covers eligible schemes and beneficiaries, requirements under the annexes, derogations and conditions governing access to support.

section: Article 13 — Financial support for corporate vehicles
category: EU-origin eligibility for corporate vehicle support
summary: Links the 'made in the European Union' criterion for corporate vehicle support to Annex III. Covers the eligibility requirements and conditions attached to financial support for corporate cars and vans.

section: Article 14 — CO2 emission performance standards credits
category: Vehicle emissions credits and EU-origin criteria
summary: Links treatment under vehicle CO2 standards to the relevant EU-origin requirements. Covers eligibility for credits, vehicle and material criteria, and the conditions governing their use under the vehicle emissions framework.

section: Article 15 — Certification of a vehicle's compliance with Union origin requirements
category: Vehicle origin certification and verification
summary: Requires vehicle manufacturers to indicate compliance with EU-origin requirements when issuing certificates of conformity. Covers certification duties, implementation timing and evidence or verification arrangements.

category: Demand measures and adjustment of product requirements
summary: Empowers the Commission to introduce chemical-sector demand measures and adjust Annex II and III requirements. Covers sustainable carbon sources, sectoral coverage, criteria for changing requirements, calculation methods and verification tools.

section: Article 17 — Scope of foreign investment contribution
category: Investment thresholds, sectors and exemptions
summary: Defines which foreign investments fall under Chapter IV, including the EUR 100 million threshold, emerging strategic manufacturing sectors and relevant third-country capacity conditions. Covers exemptions and changes to the investments or sectors subject to review.

section: Article 18 — Value added foreign direct investment criteria
category: Industrial benefits and conditions for foreign investment
summary: Sets approval criteria concerning ownership, joint ventures, intellectual property, research spending, EU employment and domestic sourcing. Also establishes national Investment Authorities and rules for applying conditions to subsidiaries and verifying compliance.

section: Article 19 — Prior notification of planned foreign direct investments
category: Investment notification and information requirements
summary: Requires advance notification of covered investments to national Investment Authorities. Covers notification timing, information to be submitted, communication with the Commission and other authorities, and handling of confidential information.

category: National investment review and approval procedures
summary: Governs national assessment of notified investments and compliance with approval conditions. Covers admissibility, review deadlines, approval decisions, investor commitments and communication of outcomes.

section: Article 21 — Review of foreign direct investment by the Commission
category: Commission intervention in investment assessments
summary: Sets the circumstances in which the Commission may assess an investment. Covers EU-level review triggers, coordination with national authorities, assessment procedures and the resulting decisions.

section: Article 22 — Monitoring and enforcement by the Investment Authority
category: Enforcement of foreign investment conditions
summary: Requires national authorities to monitor continuing compliance with investment conditions. Covers information requests, corrective measures, non-compliance consequences, penalties and the powers needed to enforce investment decisions.

category: Monitoring global capacity and investment risks
summary: Requires Commission monitoring of global manufacturing capacity in emerging strategic sectors. Covers evidence used to identify relevant third-country capacity, information gathering and implementation of the investment framework.

section: Article 24 — Delegation of powers for foreign investment
category: Updating the sectors covered by investment conditions
summary: Empowers the Commission to supplement the emerging strategic sectors subject to foreign investment conditions. Covers the criteria, safeguards and procedures for extending sectoral coverage.

section: Article 25 — Designating national industrial manufacturing acceleration areas
category: Designation and scope of acceleration areas
summary: Requires Member States to designate industrial manufacturing acceleration areas. Covers location, strategic-sector eligibility, designation criteria, infrastructure and environmental considerations, consultation and the role of Commission guidance.

category: Infrastructure, energy and support in acceleration areas
summary: Sets measures to facilitate activity in acceleration areas, including infrastructure, energy and resource access, investment support and industrial cooperation. Covers practical conditions for developing and operating industrial projects in those areas.

section: Article 27 — Permit-granting procedures in acceleration areas
category: Area-wide permits and project authorisation
summary: Introduces aggregated baseline permits for designated acceleration areas and related project procedures. Covers the relationship between area-level assessment and individual authorisations, procedural deadlines and applicable safeguards.

category: Monitoring outcomes and evaluation criteria
summary: Requires periodic evaluation of the Regulation. Covers reporting intervals and assessment of its effects on industrial capacity, competitiveness, resilience, decarbonisation and other proposed performance indicators.

category: Review of demand measures and investment rules
summary: Provides for review of Chapters III and IV and possible changes to the framework. Covers review timing, evidence requirements, sectoral coverage and assessment of the need to maintain or adapt the measures.

category: Parliamentary and Council scrutiny of delegated acts
summary: Sets conditions for the Commission's delegated powers, including their duration, revocation and objections by Parliament or Council. Covers the institutional safeguards governing adoption and continuation of delegated acts.

category: Comitology and the advisory procedure
summary: Establishes committee assistance for Commission implementing acts. The single amendment in this package proposes deleting paragraph 2, which refers to the advisory procedure under Regulation (EU) No 182/2011.

category: Sanctions for infringements
summary: Requires Member States to establish effective, proportionate and dissuasive penalties for infringements. Covers the sanctions framework and proposed additional enforcement or implementation requirements.

section: Article 33 — Amendments to Regulation (EU) 2018/1724 — Single Digital Gateway
category: Single Digital Gateway alignment
summary: Aligns the Single Digital Gateway annexes with industrial permitting information and procedures. No amendments directly target Article 33 in the 268–5417 package. The Commission text refers to Annex V, while the supplied annex package labels the corresponding changes Annex IV.

section: Article 34 — Amendments to Regulation (EU) 2024/1735 — Net-Zero Industry Act
category: Net-zero technology demand measures and permitting
summary: Amends the Net-Zero Industry Act across definitions, permitting, public procurement, renewable-energy auctions and other public intervention. Covers technology-specific origin and resilience requirements, eligibility, exceptions and implementation. References must distinguish Article 34 from the underlying provisions of the amended Act.

section: Article 35 — Amendments to Regulation (EU) 2024/3110 — Construction Products Regulation
category: Environmental sustainability labelling of construction products
summary: Amends the Commission's delegated powers to establish environmental sustainability labelling for construction product families and categories. Covers the scope and conditions of that labelling power.

section: Article 36 — Entry into force and application
category: Commencement and implementation dates
summary: Sets entry into force and deferred application of the single access point and permitting provisions. Covers the dates and transition periods for implementation of the Regulation.

category: Social and labour objectives
summary: Introduces social and labour obligations for operators benefiting from procurement, public support and acceleration measures, and for covered foreign investors.

category: Social conditionality of public support
summary: Proposes labour, social, environmental and human-rights conditions for access to public support, together with company obligations.

category: National competences and digital administrative flexibility
summary: Two alternative insertions address protection of national, regional and local competences and continued use of existing national digital systems for permit coordination.

category: Defence-related permitting and demand-measure scope
summary: Alternative insertions concern priority treatment for defence-related industrial projects and clarification of the products and services covered by origin and low-carbon demand measures.

category: Origin safeguards and strategic industrial policy
summary: Different insertions under the same proposed article number address anti-circumvention, economic security, sectoral action plans and the determination of software origin.

category: Anti-circumvention of origin equivalence
summary: Proposes investigations, suspension or withdrawal of equivalent-origin treatment and monitoring of trade and investment patterns that may indicate circumvention.

category: Approval of procurement equivalence for third countries
summary: Proposes requiring a unanimous Council decision before content from a third country can qualify as equivalent to Union origin for public procurement.

category: Equivalence safeguards, steel origin and recycled materials
summary: Alternative insertions cover equivalence conditions, circumvention, recycled-material market barriers, melt-and-pour origin rules for steel and a public database of equivalent-origin countries.

category: Anti-circumvention and intra-EU recycling flows
summary: Alternative insertions address exclusion from origin equivalence following circumvention and removal of disproportionate administrative barriers to intra-EU waste shipments for recycling.

category: Low-carbon labels and EU recycled-product procurement
summary: Alternative insertions propose a steel greenhouse-gas label, certification and labelling for low-carbon fertilising products, and procurement preferences for recycled products made in Europe.

category: Procurement preferences for EU recycled products
summary: Proposes procurement priority criteria for recycled products made in Europe, linking industrial demand measures to recycling objectives.

category: SME compliance and private construction requirements
summary: Three amendments propose simplified compliance tools and reporting for SMEs. A separate insertion under the same article number proposes low-carbon requirements for large private non-residential building and infrastructure contracts.

category: Low-carbon EU aluminium for vehicle credits
summary: Clarifies the meaning of low-carbon aluminium made in the EU for the vehicle CO2 performance standards framework by linking it to the Regulation's carbon and origin criteria.

category: Demand measures for the chemical industry
summary: Proposes measures applying the Chapter's objectives and instruments to the chemical industry, with stakeholder involvement and consideration of technical and economic feasibility.

category: Chemical capacity, SME support and chemicals origin
summary: Alternative insertions concern support for strategic chemical production capacity, integration of SMEs into supported industrial value chains and use of the Customs Code to determine chemicals origin.

category: Coordination with foreign investment screening
summary: Proposes a single notification, national contact point and coordinated timelines where an investment is subject to both this Regulation and foreign investment screening.

category: Investment conditions for additional net-zero technologies
summary: Proposes specific review and approval conditions for foreign investment in additional net-zero technologies, linked to selected Article 18 criteria and economic security objectives.

category: Shared investment screening contact points and guidance
summary: Proposes using contact points and guidance under the foreign investment screening framework instead of establishing separate arrangements for this Chapter.

category: EU register of investment decisions and penalties
summary: Proposes a shared register of investment decisions and penalties within the secure database used for foreign investment screening.

category: Acceleration plans and national designation powers
summary: Alternative insertions concern industrial acceleration plans accompanying area designation and preservation of national discretion over the location, extent and prioritisation of areas.

category: Strategic-project facilitation, planning and hydrogen
summary: Alternative insertions concern public-interest treatment and procedural flexibility for strategic projects, national industrial planning authorities and derogations from hydrogen electricity-sourcing requirements.

category: State aid for acceleration areas
summary: Proposes priority treatment of State aid schemes and individual aid supporting projects in industrial acceleration areas.

category: Long-term nuclear electricity supply
summary: Proposes long-term electricity supply arrangements backed by nuclear generation for businesses in industrial acceleration areas.

category: Industrial finance and energy-network access
summary: Alternative insertions propose a Strategic Industrial Finance Facility and energy and network assessments addressing grid capacity, connection timing and industrial self-consumption.

category: Worker transition support and expiry of origin requirements
summary: Alternative insertions propose support for workers affected by industrial transformation and a ten-year expiry of EU-origin requirements unless Parliament and Council extend them.

category: International trade commitments and industrial sovereignty
summary: Proposes provisions on the relationship between EU-origin preferences, economic security and the Union's international trade commitments.

section: Annex I — Strategic sectors for industrial manufacturing acceleration areas
category: Strategic-sector eligibility
summary: Lists the industrial sectors eligible for acceleration areas, including energy-intensive industries, automotive manufacturing and net-zero technologies. Amendments address the sector list, NACE classifications and proposed additions or changes to sectoral coverage.

section: Annex II — Low-carbon and Union origin requirements for energy-intensive industries
category: Material requirements, thresholds and sectoral coverage
summary: Sets low-carbon and EU-origin requirements for energy-intensive products under public procurement and public support. Amendments address steel, concrete and mortar, aluminium and proposed additional materials, minimum shares, application dates and extensions to other forms of demand.

section: Annex III — Union origin requirements for vehicles
category: Vehicle assembly, component origin and phased requirements
summary: Sets EU-origin conditions for vehicle procurement, public support, corporate vehicles and small zero-emission vehicle credits. Amendments address EU assembly, component-value shares, battery and powertrain requirements, phase-in dates, small-vehicle derogations and manufacturer-level compliance arrangements.

category: Single Digital Gateway permitting information and procedures
summary: Amends the Single Digital Gateway annexes to cover industrial permitting information, applications and outputs. No amendments directly target Annex IV in the 268–5417 package. The corresponding provision in Commission Article 33 refers to Annex V, while the annex package uses Annex IV.

category: Third-country procurement equivalence and strategic-sector lists
summary: Two competing insertions share this heading. Amendment 4706 proposes a list of third countries qualifying for procurement equivalence (labelled Annex X1 in its text). Amendment 4707 instead proposes a strategic-sector list covering selected energy-intensive industries, automotive and maritime activities.

category: Third-country equivalence for public support
summary: Amendment 4708 proposes a list of customs-union and free-trade-agreement partners whose content would qualify as equivalent to Union origin for other forms of public intervention. The inserted text labels the annex X2 and includes placeholders for agreements pending ratification.

category: Countries subject to foreign investment conditions
summary: Amendment 4709 proposes a sector-specific list of third countries whose investments would fall under Chapter IV because of their market-dominant position. It lists China for batteries, electric and related vehicles, solar photovoltaics and critical raw materials. The inserted text labels the annex X3.

category: EU-origin requirements for electric industrial machinery
summary: Amendment 5417 proposes EU-origin requirements for electric machinery used in construction, infrastructure, lifting, handling, logistics and industrial operations. It introduces conditions for public procurement and public support, including assembly and component-origin requirements.
